title: CRM for Jira
headings: Start with your role# Salesperson# Sales manager# Account or data owner# Jira administrator# How the pieces fit# Where to open it#
text: Many teams already run their work in Jira but keep their customers in a spreadsheet or a separate CRM. CRM for Jira puts the sales side next to the delivery side: you track who might buy, what you are selling and what to do next, and you can point any record at the Jira work item that delivers it. Quick start → Leads, deals and the pipeline Troubleshooting Start with your role # Salesperson # You work leads and deals every day. Quick start Leads and deals Tasks Search, filters and saved views Sales manager # You watch the pipeline and the team. Dashboard Reports Bulk actions, import and export Activities Account or data owner # You keep customer records clean. Contacts and companies Products Records, notes and timeline Potential duplicates Jira administrator # You install the app and set it up. Settings Permissions and access Limits and behaviour Privacy and security How the pieces fit # The app has one pipeline and a handful of record types. Each links to the others, so you can move from a deal to its contact, its company and its tasks without searching. Leads are people or companies that might buy. You rate them, work them and either convert or lose them. Deals are sales you are working on. They move through six stages and carry an amount, a close date and a next step. Contacts and companies are who you sell to. A contact belongs to a company, and a company can have a parent. Products are your catalogue. Attach them to a deal and its amount follows. Tasks and notes record what to do and what happened, on any record. Dashboard and reports turn all of it into numbers: what needs attention now, and how a period compares with the last one. Where to open it # Open CRM for Jira from the Apps menu in the Jira sidebar. The app has one global page with a menu on the left: Leads, Deals, Contacts, Companies, Products, Tasks, Dashboard, Activities, Reports and Settings. It does not add anything to individual Jira projects.

title: Quick start
headings: The example# Add a lead# Convert it to a deal# Work the deal# Close it# What to do next#
text: The example # These docs follow one small sale so you can trace it from page to page. You do not need the same data. Example: Northwind Traders A company called Northwind Traders asks about an annual licence. Sarah Miller is the person you talk to. You expect to sell the Team licence product for 12,000 USD and hope to close by the end of the month. Add a lead # Open CRM for Jira from the Jira Apps menu and choose Leads . Press Create Lead . Enter the name Northwind Traders: annual licence , contact Sarah Miller , her email, the source Referral and the rating Warm . Choose yourself as assignee. Press Create Lead to save. Only the name is required. Convert it to a deal # After a call, set the lead's status to Contacted , then Qualified . Open the lead and press Convert to Deal . Confirm. The lead is marked Converted and shows the new deal under Converted deal . Open Deals to see it in the New column. Converting asks you to confirm because it creates several records at once: the deal, and a contact and company if none matched. The lead's products carry over; the lead is kept for your history. Work the deal # Open the deal. Add the product Team licence (create it first under Products with a price of 12,000). The deal's amount follows its products. Set a Close date and a Next step , for example Send proposal with a due date. Move the deal to Discovery , then Proposal , using the stage selector. Add a note after each call. Add a task from the card: Call Sarah on Friday . Close it # When the customer signs, press Mark as Won and choose a reason, for example Product Fit . Open Dashboard : the deal now counts in Deals Won and in the win rate. Open Reports to see it under Won Deals by Reason and in the period comparison. If you lose a deal instead, press Mark as Lost and pick a reason. Always pick one: reports break results down by reason. What to do next # Bring in existing customers with CSV import . Set up saved views for the lists you open every day. Link a deal to the Jira work item that delivers it: Linking to Jira . Check Settings for your currency and how long before a deal counts as stale.

title: Leads, deals and the pipeline
headings: From lead to deal# The six stages# Weighted pipeline# Won and lost, and why# Stale deals#
text: From lead to deal # A lead is someone who has shown interest but is not yet a customer. A deal is a sale you are actively working. The two are separate records on purpose: most leads never become deals, and you do not want them in your forecast. A lead moves through five statuses: New , Contacted , Qualified , Converted or Lost . When a lead is qualified, you convert it. That creates the deal and links the two, so you can always see where a deal came from. The six stages # There is one pipeline, with six stages. Each has a default chance of winning: Stage Win probability Meaning New 10% Just created, not yet worked Discovery 25% You are learning what the customer needs Negotiation 50% Terms are being discussed Proposal 75% A proposal is with the customer Won 100% Closed, the customer signed Lost 0% Closed, no sale One pipeline is enough for most small teams. The stages are fixed: you cannot add or rename them. Weighted pipeline # A raw pipeline total treats a brand new deal and a nearly signed one as equal. Weighted pipeline multiplies each open deal's amount by its probability, so it is a more realistic forecast. Example Deal Amount Stage Weighted Northwind: annual licence 12,000 Proposal (75%) 9,000 Contoso: pilot 4,000 Discovery (25%) 1,000 Pipeline 16,000 10,000 If you know a particular deal is more or less likely than its stage says, set a probability on that deal. It replaces the stage's default for that deal only. Won and lost, and why # Moving a deal to Won or Lost asks for a reason. The reasons are what the Deal outcomes report counts, so they turn a hunch ("we keep losing on price") into a number. Won: Best Price, Product Fit, Relationship, Switched from Competitor, Referral, Other. Lost: Price, Lost to Competitor, No Budget, No Decision Made, Bad Timing, Other. Stale deals # A deal is stale when it has not changed stage for a number of days. The default is 14; a Jira administrator can change it in Settings . Stale deals are flagged in the board and the table, and there is a Stale filter for them. A deal that is Won or Lost is never stale. The same threshold applies to leads : a lead whose status has not changed for that long, and which is not yet Converted or Lost, is flagged stale.

title: Records, notes and timeline
headings: The record card# Tasks tab# Notes tab# Timeline tab# Deleting and merging# Sharing a card#
text: The record card # Click the name of any lead, contact, company, deal, product or task, anywhere in the app, to open its card . A card has two columns: the record's details on one side, and tabs for what has happened and what is next on the other. Besides the fields you entered, every card shows Last activity , so you can tell at a glance whether anyone has touched the record lately. A deal card also shows how long it has been in stage . Tasks tab # The tasks tied to this record. Type a title in the box, optionally a due date as YYYY-MM-DD , and add it. It appears in Tasks too. Tasks can be tied to a lead, contact, company or deal. Notes tab # Free-text notes on the record: what was said on a call, what the customer asked for. Type in the Add a note… box and add it. Notes are up to 2,000 characters, are shown with the date they were added, and are included in global search . You are asked to confirm before deleting a note. Notes can be added to leads, contacts, companies and deals. Timeline tab # Everything that happened to the record, newest first: who created it, who changed which field and from what, who reassigned it, converted it or merged into it. An edit reads like rating: Cold → Hot . Stage and status changes and owner changes get their own lines. The timeline is part of the audit trail , which keeps the latest 500 entries for the whole app. On a busy site, very old entries drop off. Deleting and merging # Deleting a contact or company that has linked records shows a warning first. If you have entered the same customer twice, use merge instead of delete: it moves everything onto the record you keep. Sharing a card # Each card has its own web address. See Sharing records .

title: Leads
headings: Add a lead# Board and table# Converting a lead# Losing a lead#
text: Add a lead # Open Leads and press Create Lead . Only the name is required. The rest helps you decide whom to call first: Field What it is for Status New, Contacted, Qualified, Converted or Lost. Rating Hot, Warm or Cold: how likely the lead is to buy. Source Where it came from: Web, Referral, Advertisement, Trade Show, Cold Call, Partner or Other. Reports use it to show which sources convert. Assignee Who is responsible. Leads with no assignee can be found with the Unassigned filter. Contact and company Link to an existing contact or company, or just type the names. Email, phone Checked for a sensible format. Two leads (or contacts) cannot share one email address. Jira work item Optional. See Linking to Jira . A lead can also carry products , the things the prospect asked about. They carry over when you convert. Board and table # Switch between Table and Kanban with the buttons above the list. The board has a column per status. The table has sortable columns (click a heading) and the same quick filters as everywhere: see Search, filters and saved views . The tiles above the list, such as My Leads and Unassigned , are filters too. Converting a lead # Open the lead and press Convert to Deal , then confirm. The app: creates a deal in the New stage, with an amount equal to the lead's products; uses the lead's contact and company if they are linked, or finds a company with the same name, or creates a new contact and company from the names on the lead; carries over the lead's products; marks the lead Converted and links the two records both ways. The lead's card then shows the Converted deal , and you can open it from there. Losing a lead # Set the status to Lost and choose a reason: Unqualified, No Response, Not Interested, Duplicate, Wrong Contact or Other. Reports count lost leads by reason, so a vague "Other" is a missed chance to learn something.

title: Deals
headings: Add a deal# Board and table# Products on a deal# Winning and losing# Deleting a deal#
text: Add a deal # Open Deals and press Create Deal , or convert a lead . Fields: Field What it is for Name Required. Amount Zero or more, in the currency set in Settings . Once you attach products, the amount follows them. Stage One of the six stages . Close date When you expect to close. Used by the forecast by month. A deal past its close date is flagged overdue. Next step and its due date What happens next. Deals with no next step can be found with the No Next Step filter. Type New Business, Existing Business or Renewal. Win probability Optional. Replaces the stage's default for this deal. Contact, company Who you are selling to. Owner Who is responsible for the deal. Jira work item Optional. See Linking to Jira . Dates are typed as YYYY-MM-DD , for example 2026-11-30 . The app has no date picker. Board and table # Deals open as a Kanban board: one column per stage, with the number of deals and their total value at the top of each. Press Table view for a sortable list and Kanban view to go back. Stale deals carry a badge showing how many days they have sat in their stage. Cards cannot be dragged between columns. Change the stage with the stage selector on the card or in the table row. Products on a deal # Open a deal and add products from your catalogue as line items. The deal's amount is kept in step with the line items, so you do not have to add them up. A line item keeps the price it had when you added it, so changing the catalogue price later does not rewrite existing deals. Winning and losing # Press Mark as Won and choose a reason. The stage becomes Won . Press Mark as Lost and choose a reason. The stage becomes Lost . The reasons feed Deal outcomes . Won deals count in the Dashboard's Deals Won and in the win rate. Deleting a deal # You are asked to confirm. Deleting removes the deal's line items and notes with it. The deal's history stays in Activities until it ages out.

title: Contacts and companies
headings: Contacts# Companies# Merging duplicates# Deleting#
text: Contacts # A contact is a person. Open Contacts and press the create button. Only the name is required. Field Notes Title Their job title. Email, secondary email, phone Checked for a sensible format. Two contacts cannot share one email address. LinkedIn A link to their profile. Company The company they work for. Reports to Another contact, so you can see who works for whom. Tags Comma-separated, for example partner, conference . Do not contact Tick it for people who must not be contacted. A quick filter shows or hides them. Owner Who looks after the relationship. Companies # A company is an organisation. Fields: website, industry, address (city, state, ZIP, country), employees, annual revenue, LinkedIn, tags, owner and a Parent company so you can model subsidiaries. A company's card lists the contacts who work there and the deals attached to it. Reports group companies by industry and by size. Merging duplicates # If the same person or company has been entered twice: Open the duplicate you want to get rid of. Choose Merge into and pick the record to keep. Press Merge and Delete . Everything that pointed at the duplicate (deals, leads, tasks, notes and, for companies, contacts) now points at the record you kept. Merging cannot be undone. To find candidates, open Reports → Potential Duplicates . Deleting # Deleting a contact or company that has linked deals, tasks or contacts shows a warning that lists what will be affected, so nothing disappears by accident.

title: Products
headings: The catalogue# Using products# Deleting a product#
text: The catalogue # Open Products and create a product for each thing you sell. Fields: Field Notes Name Required. SKU Your own code for the product. Two products with the same SKU show up under Potential Duplicates . Price What you charge. Zero or more. Cost What it costs you. The list shows the margin from price and cost. Category Free text, used to group products in reports. Unit License, Service, Project, Subscription or One-time. Description Free text. Using products # Attach products to a lead or a deal as line items. A product's own card shows which deals use it . The Unused filter lists products no deal uses yet, which is handy for tidying the catalogue. Revenue reports group won deals by product and by category: see Reports → Revenue . Deleting a product # You are asked to confirm. Products can be deleted in bulk: see Bulk actions .

title: Tasks
headings: Add a task# Working your list# Deleting#
text: Add a task # Open Tasks and press Create Task , or add one from the Tasks tab of any record. Fields: Field Notes Title Required. Type To-do, Call, Email, Meeting or Other. Priority High, Normal or Low. Due A date as YYYY-MM-DD . Assignee Who has to do it. Related to A lead, contact, company or deal. Notes Anything else worth knowing. Working your list # A task is open until you complete it. The filters keep your day under control: My Tasks : only those assigned to you. Overdue : past their due date and still open. Due Today . By priority and by type. The side menu shows a number next to Tasks when something needs attention, and the Dashboard lists tasks due soon. Select several tasks to change their priority or assignee at once: see Bulk actions . Deleting # You are asked to confirm before a task is deleted from a record's card.

title: Search, filters and saved views
headings: Search# Global search# Filters# Saved views#
text: Search # Each list has its own search box above it, which searches that section by name and other key fields. Global search # The box at the top of the app searches every section at once , including the text of notes. Type at least two characters. Results are grouped by record type with the number of matches in each; click one to open its card. Filters # Quick filters sit above each list. Which ones you see depends on the section: Section Quick filters Leads My Leads, Unassigned, status, rating, source, stale Deals My Deals, Stale, Overdue, No Next Step, Unassigned, stage, type Contacts My Contacts, Do Not Contact, Unlinked (no company), company Companies My Companies, industry, With Open Deals Products Unused, category, unit Tasks My Tasks, Overdue, Due Today, priority, type The numbered tiles above a list are filters too. Click a tile and the list narrows to exactly those rows; click it again to clear it. The Dashboard tiles work the same way and open the right list already filtered. To sort, click a column heading. Saved views # When you have filters set, a Save view button appears. Give the view a name (up to 60 characters) and press Save . It shows up as a button above the list: click it to bring those filters back, or press × next to it to delete it. Saved views are yours alone . Colleagues do not see them. A view is a set of filters for one section. It does not freeze the data: the same view next week shows next week's rows. There is nothing to save until a filter is on, so the button is hidden on an unfiltered list. Example On Deals , turn on My Deals and Stale , then save the view as My stale deals . Every Monday, one click shows what to chase.

title: Bulk actions, import and export
headings: Bulk actions# Import from CSV# Export to CSV#
text: Bulk actions # Tick the boxes at the start of rows to select them. Buttons for the actions available in that section appear above the list. Section You can Leads Assign, change status, change rating, delete Deals Assign owner, change stage, delete Contacts, Companies Assign owner, delete Products Delete Tasks Assign, change priority, complete, delete Deleting asks you to confirm and states how many records will go. Bulk deletion cannot be undone. Import from CSV # Press Import CSV on Contacts, Companies, Leads, Deals, Products or Tasks. In your spreadsheet, make the first row the column names , then export or copy it as CSV text. Paste the text into the window. It lists the column names it recognises; use those names exactly. Press Import . Each row is checked exactly as if you had typed it into the form. A row with, say, an invalid email address is skipped and listed with the reason; the other rows are still imported. Only the name is required. Example: importing contacts Name Title Company Email Phone Tags Sarah Miller Head of Operations Northwind Traders sarah@example.com +1 555 0100 partner The columns it recognises for contacts are Name , Title , Company , Email , Secondary Email , Phone , LinkedIn , Tags and Jira Work Item . A company is matched by name to one that already exists, so import companies first. Import twice and you get two copies. Import does not look for existing records. Check the result, and use Potential Duplicates if you have to clean up. Export to CSV # Press Export CSV on a list. A window shows the data as text: select all (Ctrl+A or Cmd+A), copy, and paste it into a spreadsheet or a file ending in .csv . The export follows your current filters. If rows are selected, you can export just those. Several report tables have their own Export to CSV button, and Settings can export everything. The app shows CSV as text, not as a download, because the page it runs in cannot start a file download.

title: Dashboard
headings: What is on it# Tiles are shortcuts# How the key numbers are worked out#
text: What is on it # The Dashboard answers "what needs me today?" before "how are we doing?". Its sections: Section What it shows Needs attention Counts of things to act on: overdue tasks, overdue next steps, deals past their close date, stale deals, stale leads and potential duplicates. Totals How many leads, contacts, companies and deals you have. Pipeline Open deals, open pipeline value, weighted pipeline and average deal. Performance For a chosen period (7, 30 or 90 days, or all time), and optionally one assignee: won value, deals won and lost, win rate, new leads, average deal and sales cycle. With a period chosen, each tile shows the change against the period before it. Pipeline by stage How many deals and how much value sit in each stage. Deals Closing Soon, Tasks Due Soon The next things on the calendar. Recently Won, Recent Activity What just happened. Trends New leads, revenue and win rate over the last few months. Tiles are shortcuts # A tile that names a group of records is a filter. Click Stale or No Next Step and you land on the Deals list already narrowed to exactly those deals. Use it as a daily starting point. How the key numbers are worked out # Win rate : deals won divided by deals won plus lost in the period. Open deals are not counted. With no closed deals it shows a dash rather than 0%. Sales cycle : the average time from creating a deal to winning it, for deals won in the period. Weighted pipeline : see Leads, deals and the pipeline . The currency of every amount comes from Settings .

title: Reports
headings: Reports and the period# Compare with the previous period# Report snapshot# Pipeline# Leads# Revenue# Deal outcomes# Accounts, products and operations# Data quality#
text: Reports and the period # Open Reports . The page is a set of cards in sections. Pick a period at the top ( This month , Last month , This quarter , This year or Last 30 days ) to see the figures that depend on time. Compare with the previous period # The comparison card sets the chosen period against the one before it: won value , deals won , deals lost , win rate and deals created , with the change in each. For win rate the change is in percentage points. It can be exported to CSV. Report snapshot # Press Report snapshot for a short text summary of the period. Select it all (Ctrl+A or Cmd+A), copy it and paste it into a Jira comment, a Confluence page or a chat message; they all display it formatted. It is a good way to put the week's numbers in front of people who do not open the app. Pipeline # Deals by Stage and Pipeline Value by Stage Forecast by Close Month : expected value by the deals' close dates Open Pipeline by Owner Average Days per Stage : where deals wait Deals by Type Leads # Leads by Status, Source and Rating Conversion Rate by Source and by Rating : which sources and ratings really turn into deals Lost Leads by Reason Revenue # Revenue by Lead Source , by Product and by Category : what won deals brought in Sales Performance by Assignee , with CSV export Deal outcomes # Won Deals by Reason and Lost Deals by Reason . These are only as good as the reasons people choose when they close a deal. Accounts, products and operations # Companies by Industry and by Size Products by Category and Deal Contacts by Product (who bought what) Tasks by Type , by Priority and Task Load by Assignee Data quality # Potential Duplicates lists records that probably describe the same thing: companies with the same name or website, contacts with the same email or phone, products with the same SKU. Open each and merge where it is a real duplicate. Reports are calculated from the records in the app at the moment you open them, so they are always current. They can be a little slow on a site with a lot of data: see Limits and behaviour .

title: Activities
headings: What is logged# Where to see it# How much is kept#
text: What is logged # Every change in the app writes one line to the audit trail: who did it, what they did, to which record , and when . Events are of these kinds: Created, Updated, Status changed, Reassigned, Note added, Converted, Merged and Deleted. An edit lists the fields that changed, with before and after, for example rating: Cold → Hot, amount: 8,000 → 12,000 . If many fields changed, the first few are shown with a count of the rest. A change to a field that points at another record, such as the company, is reported as company changed . Where to see it # The Activities section: everything, newest first. Filter by record type (Lead, Contact, Company, Deal, Product, Task) and by event type. A record's Timeline tab : only that record's history. Last activity on a card and Recent Activity on the Dashboard. Activities can be exported to CSV. How much is kept # The trail keeps the latest 500 entries . Older ones are removed automatically as new ones arrive, so it is a recent history, not a permanent archive. The Activities section shows the newest 100. Settings shows how many entries are kept right now. If you need a long-term record of something, put it in a note on the record.

title: Settings
headings: Workspace settings# Data administration# Audit log#
text: Workspace settings # Setting What it does Workspace Currency USD, EUR, GBP, JPY or INR. It changes the symbol amounts are shown with, everywhere. It does not convert anything: an amount of 1,000 stays 1,000 and is simply shown in the new currency. Stale Threshold (days) How many days a deal can sit in a stage, or a lead in a status, before it is flagged stale . A whole number from 1 to 365. The default is 14. Press Save after changing a setting. Settings apply to everyone on the Jira site, so only a Jira administrator can change them; see Permissions and access . Data administration # Export all of your records from here, section by section, as CSV text. Use it for a backup or to move data into another tool. Audit log # Shows how many activity entries are kept right now, out of the 500 the app holds.

title: Linking to Jira and sharing records
headings: Linking a record to a work item# Sharing records#
text: Linking a record to a work item # Leads, contacts, companies and deals have a Jira work item field. Type a key such as PROJ-123 and save. The app checks the item as you : it must exist and you must be allowed to see it. If it does, the record then shows the item's summary and status next to the key, so a deal can point at the ticket that delivers it. The key is looked up at the moment you save; a later change to the item's summary or status is not pulled in until you save the record again. Keys are not case sensitive: proj-123 is stored as PROJ-123 . If the key does not exist, or you cannot see it, the save is refused with a message. The app only reads the work item. It never changes anything in Jira. Sharing records # Every record card has its own web address. When you open a card, the address in your browser changes to point at it, and changes back when you close it. Copy it from the address bar and paste it into a Jira comment, an email or a chat message; whoever opens it (and has access to the app) lands directly on the same record. The address carries the record's id in a parameter named for its section: selectedDealId , selectedLeadId , selectedContactId , selectedCompanyId , selectedProductId or selectedTaskId . If you open a link to a record that has since been deleted, the app opens normally and there is no card to show.

title: Limits and behaviour
headings: Limits# How much data is comfortable# Behaviour#
text: Limits # What Limit What happens at the limit Length of a text field (name, title, address and so on) 255 Anything longer is cut off when saved. Length of a note 2,000 Cut off when saved. Length of a saved view's name 60 Refused. Stale threshold 1–365 days Refused outside the range. Entries kept in the audit trail 500 The oldest are removed as new ones arrive. See Activities . Activities shown on screen 100 The newest 100 of those kept. Search results per record type 10 The count of all matches is still shown. How much data is comfortable # The app loads your records when it opens and does the searching, sorting and filtering in your browser. That makes it quick and simple for a small team. It also means that the more records you have, the longer it takes to open, and the longer reports take to calculate. A few thousand records per section is comfortable. If the app starts to feel slow to open or to save, tell your administrator and contact support . Pages that need to look at everything, such as global search, Potential Duplicates and some of the revenue reports, feel it first. Behaviour # Topic How it behaves Currency One currency for the whole workspace, set in Settings. Amounts are never converted. Pipeline One pipeline with six fixed stages. They cannot be renamed or added to. Dates Typed as YYYY-MM-DD . There is no date picker. Phone numbers 7 to 20 characters: digits, spaces, + - ( ) . Email addresses Must look like an email. Two contacts, or two leads, cannot share one. Amounts and prices Zero or more. Drag and drop Not available. Change a deal's stage with its selector. Export and import CSV as text you copy and paste, not as a file download. Saved views Belong to the person who made them. Deleting Permanent. There is no recycle bin. Jira data Only read, never changed. See Privacy .

title: Permissions and access
headings: Who can do what# What the app asks of Jira#
text: Who can do what # The app has no roles of its own . Anyone who can open the app can see and change every record in it: there is no private lead, deal or contact. Treat access to the app as access to your whole customer list. Action Any user of the app Jira administrator View records, reports and the audit trail Yes Yes Create, edit, delete and merge records Yes Yes Import, export, bulk actions Yes Yes Save your own views Yes Yes Change Settings (currency, stale threshold) No Yes Owner and assignee are labels that say who is responsible. They do not restrict who can edit the record. Who can open the app at all is controlled by Jira: the Apps menu entry is available to people who can use Jira on the site. What the app asks of Jira # Installing the app asks a Jira administrator to approve three permissions: Permission What it is used for storage:app The app's own storage, where your records are kept. read:jira-work Checking that a work item key you type exists and showing its summary and status. read:jira-user Showing people's names and searching for people in the owner and assignee pickers. The app has no permission to create, edit or comment on anything in Jira. Every Jira lookup is made as the signed-in user, so it sees only what that person can see.

title: Glossary
text: Amount The value of a deal, in the workspace currency. Follows the deal's products once any are attached. Assignee The person responsible for a lead or a task. Audit trail The log of who changed what and when. Also called Activities. The latest 500 entries are kept. Card The panel that opens when you click a record's name, with its details, tasks, notes and timeline. Close date When you expect a deal to close. Drives the forecast by month and the overdue flag. Company An organisation you sell to. Can have a parent company. Contact A person at a company, or on their own. Convert Turning a qualified lead into a deal. Creates a contact and company if none match. Deal A sale you are working on, moving through the pipeline. Deal type New Business, Existing Business or Renewal. Kanban The board view, with a column per stage (deals) or status (leads). Lead A prospect who has shown interest but is not yet a customer. Line item A product attached to a lead or deal. Keeps the price it had when added. Next step What happens next on a deal, with an optional due date. Owner The person responsible for a deal, contact or company. Pipeline All your open deals, by stage. The total value of open deals is the open pipeline. Win probability The chance a deal will be won. Each stage has a default; a deal can override it. Rating Hot, Warm or Cold: how likely a lead is to buy. Saved view A named set of filters on one list, kept for you alone. Sales cycle The average days from creating a deal to winning it. SKU Your own code for a product. Stage Where a deal is: New, Discovery, Negotiation, Proposal, Won or Lost. Stale A deal or lead that has not moved for longer than the stale threshold. Timeline A record's own history, on its card. Weighted pipeline Each open deal's amount multiplied by its win probability, added up. Win rate Deals won divided by deals won plus lost. Work item Jira's name for an issue. A record can store one work item key.

title: Troubleshooting
headings: Saving and entering data# A record will not save# Saving seems slow# I cannot change Settings# Records and lists# A list is empty but I know the records exist# The deals board is not what I expected# A deal's amount changed on its own# Converting a lead made a contact and a company I did not expect# I deleted or merged something by mistake# Numbers# The Dashboard and a report show different numbers# Win rate shows a dash# The currency looks wrong# The Activities list is missing older changes# Import and export# Import skipped some rows# Import created duplicates# A company or contact did not link on import# Links# A link to a record opens the app but not the record#
text: Find the symptom, check the cause, follow the fix. If nothing here helps, see support . Saving and entering data # A record will not save # Check What to do Is the name filled in? It is the only required field on most records. Does the message mention an email? The address must look like an email, and two contacts or two leads cannot share one. Find the existing record with search. Does it mention a phone number? Use 7 to 20 characters: digits, spaces and + - ( ) . Is it a Jira work item key? It must look like PROJ-123 , exist, and be visible to you. See Linking to Jira . Is it a date? Type it as YYYY-MM-DD , for example 2026-11-30 . Saving seems slow # Cause: a save goes to the server and back before the window closes. Fix: wait for the window to close. Pressing the button again can create a second copy. If saves are consistently slow, see how much data is comfortable . I cannot change Settings # Cause: only a Jira administrator can. Fix: ask one. See Permissions and access . Records and lists # A list is empty but I know the records exist # Cause: a filter or a search is still on. Fix: clear the search box and click any highlighted tile or filter to turn it off. A saved view you clicked earlier also sets filters. The deals board is not what I expected # A deal shows in the column of its stage . If one is missing, check the Lost and Won columns at the end. Filters apply to the board as well as the table. You cannot drag cards. Use the stage selector. A deal's amount changed on its own # Cause: once a deal has products attached, its amount follows them. Fix: change the line items, not the amount. Converting a lead made a contact and a company I did not expect # Cause: converting uses the lead's linked contact and company, or a company with the same name; if there is none, it creates them from the names on the lead. Fix: link the lead to existing records before converting, or merge afterwards. I deleted or merged something by mistake # Neither can be undone, because the app has no recycle bin. The audit trail shows what was removed and by whom, so you can re-enter it. Numbers # The Dashboard and a report show different numbers # The Dashboard's performance tiles use 7, 30 or 90 days or all time; reports use calendar periods such as This month . Check the period on both. A Dashboard filtered to one assignee only counts that person. Win rate shows a dash # Cause: no deals were won or lost in the period, so there is nothing to divide. Open deals are not counted. The currency looks wrong # Cause: changing the currency in Settings changes the symbol only; it does not convert. An amount entered as 1,000 euros is now shown as 1,000 dollars. Fix: change the currency back, or re-enter the amounts. The Activities list is missing older changes # Cause: only the latest 500 entries are kept. See how much is kept . Import and export # Import skipped some rows # The result lists each skipped row with the reason. The usual causes are a missing name, an invalid email or phone number, or an email that already exists. Fix those rows and import only them again. Import created duplicates # Cause: import does not look for existing records, so a second import adds a second copy. Fix: open Reports → Potential Duplicates and merge. A company or contact did not link on import # Cause: the name must match an existing company or contact exactly (capital letters do not matter). Fix: import companies first, and check spelling. Links # A link to a record opens the app but not the record # Cause: the record was deleted, or the link was cut when copied. Fix: copy the address again from the open card, in full.

title: FAQ and support
headings: Support#
text: Do I need a separate login? No. You use your Jira account. Open the app from the Apps menu. Does the app change anything in Jira? No. It only reads: a work item's summary and status when you link one, and people's names. It never creates, edits or comments on a Jira issue. Can I see only my own records? You can filter to yours with My Leads, My Deals and the like, but the app has no per-record privacy. Everyone who can open it sees everything. See Permissions and access . Can I add my own stages or have more than one pipeline? No. There is one pipeline with six fixed stages. See Leads, deals and the pipeline . Can I drag deals between columns? No. Use the stage selector on the card or in the table row. Can I send email or log meetings from the app? No. The app does not connect to email or a calendar and does not store attachments. Write what happened as a note, and add a task for what comes next. Can I move my data in from a spreadsheet? Yes, with CSV import for contacts, companies, leads, deals, products and tasks. See Import from CSV . Can I get my data out? Yes. Export CSV from any list, or everything from Settings. See Bulk actions, import and export . Does changing the currency convert my amounts? No. It only changes the symbol. There is one currency for the whole workspace. What happens if two people edit the same record? The last save wins. The timeline shows who changed what, so you can see it happened. Can I undo a delete or a merge? No. Both are permanent. The audit trail shows what was removed. How many records can it hold? A few thousand per section is comfortable. See Limits and behaviour . Where is the data stored? In Atlassian's storage for the app, on your own Atlassian site. See the privacy policy . Support # Questions, bug reports or feature requests: info@vudia.site . To help us answer quickly, tell us which section you were in, what you expected, what you saw, and attach a screenshot if you can. Security reports go to the address on the security page .

title: What's new
headings: September 2026# August 2026#
text: September 2026 # Stat tiles are filters. Click a tile on the Dashboard or above a list and the list narrows to exactly those rows. Report snapshot. A pasteable text summary of the period for a Jira comment, a Confluence page or a chat. Period comparison in Reports. Won value, deals won and lost, win rate and deals created against the period before. Saved views. Name the filters you use and bring them back with one click. Bulk actions. Assign owners, change stages, status, rating or priority, complete or delete many records at once. Deep links. Every record card has its own address you can paste into a Jira comment. Tasks, notes and timeline as tabs on every record card, laid out in two columns. Audit trail with before and after values. Edits now read like rating: Cold → Hot . The trail keeps the latest 500 entries. New quick filters: Unassigned and No Next Step on Deals, Do Not Contact on Contacts, Unused on Products. Merge duplicate contacts and companies. CSV import and export on every list. Global search across all sections, including notes. Jira work item links on leads, contacts, companies and deals. Deal and lead details: next step, close date, type, win probability and weighted pipeline, won and lost reasons, lead source and rating, stale flags. Company hierarchy (parent and subsidiaries) and contact reporting lines . Products catalogue with line items on leads and deals. Tasks with type, priority, due date and assignee. Dashboard and Reports . August 2026 # First version: contacts, companies and deals with a Kanban pipeline.

title: Privacy policy
headings: Summary# What it reads from Jira# What it writes to Jira# What it stores# Atlassian account data# Retention & deletion# Where data is stored# Logs# Analytics & tracking# Your rights# Changes to this policy# Contact#
text: Summary # CRM for Jira is built on Atlassian Forge and runs entirely on Atlassian's infrastructure. It has no servers of its own and makes no outbound network call to anything outside Atlassian. We do not operate any system that receives your data, and we cannot see the data your site holds in the app. The app stores the records your users enter (leads, contacts, companies, deals, products, tasks and notes) in Forge storage, scoped to your own site. What it reads from Jira # Always live, using the signed-in user's own Jira permissions: A work item's key, summary and status, when a user links a record to it People's display names and profiles, to show who owns, assigned or changed a record User search results, for the owner and assignee pickers Whether the user holds the site's ADMINISTER permission, to gate the workspace settings None of it is copied anywhere outside your site. What it writes to Jira # Nothing. The app never creates, edits, transitions or comments on a Jira issue. It only reads. What it stores # In Forge storage, scoped to your site: the leads, contacts, companies, deals, products, tasks, notes and product line items your users create, the audit trail (the latest 500 entries), each person's saved views, and the workspace settings (currency and stale-deal threshold). Contacts, companies and leads can include the personal details of your customers and prospects, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, job titles and LinkedIn links. That data belongs to you: you decide what to enter, and you are responsible for having a lawful basis to keep it. passwords API tokens payment details Jira issue content beyond what's listed above Atlassian account data # The app stores the Atlassian account ID of the people who appear on records: the owner or assignee, and the person who created or last changed a record or made an audit-trail entry. It stores display names only for the moment they are shown. It stores no Atlassian email address, password or token. Retention & deletion # Data stays in your site's Forge storage until your users delete it in the app, or until the app is uninstalled. Deleting a record in the app is permanent. Deleting a deal also deletes its line items and notes; the audit trail keeps a line saying it was deleted until that line ages out. Removal of storage after uninstall follows Atlassian's own Forge retention policy. Where data is stored # Inside Atlassian's own Forge storage platform, in the same data residency as the rest of your Jira site. Nothing leaves Atlassian's infrastructure: the app declares no permission to call any external service. Logs # The app writes very little to logs, for example the number of old audit entries it removed. It does not write the contents of records to logs. Analytics & tracking # None. The app contains no analytics, no tracking pixels, no advertising and no third-party scripts of any kind. Your rights # Because we hold no copy of your data outside your own Forge storage, requests to access, correct or delete it are handled directly in the app by your own users and administrators. Anyone who can open the app can find, edit and delete a person's record. If you have a question we have not answered here, contact us using the details below. Changes to this policy # If what the app reads, writes or stores changes, this page changes with it. Contact # info@vudia.site

title: Security policy
headings: Architecture and hosting# Data we handle# Authentication and access control# Input handling# Reporting a vulnerability#
text: Architecture and hosting # CRM for Jira is built entirely on Atlassian Forge, in UI Kit (not Custom UI), so its interface is rendered by the platform itself, not by code we serve. It has no servers, databases or infrastructure of its own: it stores no data outside Atlassian, and its manifest declares no permission to make an outbound network call to anything other than Atlassian's own APIs. Transport security, encryption, physical security and patching of the underlying platform are Atlassian's responsibility, covered by Atlassian's own compliance programme for Forge. Data we handle # The app handles the records your users type in. It reads a Jira work item's summary and status live when a user links one, and people's names to display. It holds no permission to create, edit, transition or comment on an issue, so it cannot write to Jira at all. Full detail on what is and is not kept is in the privacy policy . Authentication and access control # There is no independent login system. Every request runs as the signed-in Jira user, authenticated by Forge through their existing Jira session. We never collect, transmit or store Atlassian usernames, passwords or API tokens. Inside the app there are no roles: anyone who can open it can read and change every record (see Permissions and access ). The one exception is workspace settings, which the server only accepts from a user who holds Jira's site ADMINISTER permission, checked on every save. Access is bounded by the scopes declared in the manifest: read:jira-work check that a work item exists and read its summary and status read:jira-user show people's names, search users for the owner and assignee pickers storage:app the app's own Forge key-value store No Jira write scope is declared anywhere in the manifest. Every Jira call is made as the signed-in user ( asUser ), so Jira's own permissions apply. Input handling # Every server function validates what it receives before using it: record ids must be well-formed UUIDs, text is trimmed and length-limited, choices (stages, statuses, sources, ratings, reasons, currencies) are checked against fixed lists, numbers must be finite and non-negative, and account ids and Jira work item keys must match strict patterns. Saved-view filters are limited to a fixed set of keys. The app was reviewed against the OWASP list of common weaknesses and hardened where needed. Reporting a vulnerability # Email security@vudia.site with what you found, the steps to reproduce it, and which part of the app it affects. Please do not publish details until we have had a chance to fix it. For general support, use info@vudia.site .
